# Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview

This project aims to build a data visualization tool that presents Ottoman legal and administrative records in the style of **Cerîde-i Adliyye** (The Journal of Justice) — an official Ottoman gazette published by the Ministry of Justice that recorded legal proceedings, court decisions, and judicial appointments.

## Inspiration

This project was inspired by the [Poetic Justice](https://casualarchivist.substack.com/p/poetic-justice) article on Casual Archivist, which explores the Cerîde-i Adliyye as a historical source and highlights the value of making its data accessible and visually compelling.

## Goals

- Parse and structure data drawn from Ottoman judicial records.
- Display that data in a visual style faithful to the aesthetic of Cerîde-i Adliyye.
- Make the records searchable, browsable, and legible to a modern audience.
- Respect the historical and cultural context of Ottoman legal history.

## Guidelines for Copilot

- Keep code modular and well-documented so that contributors unfamiliar with Ottoman history can still understand the data pipeline.
- When generating UI components, prefer layouts and typography that evoke the look of historical Ottoman print publications (e.g., structured columns, formal typographic hierarchy).
- Use clear, descriptive variable and function names that reflect the domain (e.g., names related to court records, judicial entries, gazette issues).
- Avoid anachronistic terminology; prefer neutral, scholarly language when naming things related to historical content.
- Tests should cover both data-processing logic and, where applicable, rendering behavior.
